coding: Single-analyst descriptive profiles of selected formulations. These are not numerical complexity scores, a census of ontologies, or a 2026 review of each field's empirical status.

profiles.name: Newtonian point-particle mechanics
profiles.primitives: Particle positions and velocities, masses, Euclidean space and time.
profiles.machinery: Second-order ordinary differential equations; conservation laws when the forces admit the corresponding symmetries.
profiles.choices: N, masses, force or potential, and initial conditions. The framework does not select every force law.
profiles.closure: Task-ready after those inputs and regularity assumptions are specified.
profiles.scope: Particle motion in its classical regime; no quantum or relativistic completion in this variant.
profiles.computation: A short law can generate difficult many-body dynamics. Runtime depends on the task, N, accuracy and time horizon.
profiles.comparison: A narrower primitive vocabulary than the complete EFMW catalogue; this does not provide a common-scale numerical rank.

profiles.name: Classical Maxwell electrodynamics
profiles.primitives: Electric and magnetic fields, or an electromagnetic potential modulo gauge, and charge-current sources.
profiles.machinery: Linear field equations in vacuum, differential identities, gauge freedom and boundary conditions.
profiles.choices: Sources, initial/boundary data and units; material constitutive functions are additional choices if matter is included.
profiles.closure: Task-ready for compatible prescribed sources and boundary data; dynamical matter needs its own equations.
profiles.computation: Partial differential equations; discretization and geometry control computational cost.
profiles.comparison: The EFMW catalogue already includes the Maxwell Lagrangian as ME-012. Reusing it does not create another independent fundamental law.

profiles.name: General relativity
profiles.variant: Einstein-Hilbert gravity with cosmological constant and specified matter
profiles.primitives: A Lorentzian metric, manifold and matter fields.
profiles.machinery: Tensor geometry, nonlinear field equations, constraints and diffeomorphism freedom.
profiles.choices: G and cosmological constant in a fixed unit convention, matter model, topology and initial/boundary data.
profiles.closure: Specified initial-value problems admit a precise formulation; global behavior and singular limits need additional analysis.
profiles.scope: Classical gravitation and spacetime; this row does not claim quantum completion.
profiles.computation: Gauge fixing, constraints and nonlinear numerical evolution can be demanding despite a compact tensor equation.
profiles.comparison: EFMW's gravitational extension inherits this burden and adds a proposed informational source whose independent definition and conservation are open in the frozen review.

profiles.name: Minimal Standard Model
profiles.variant: Renormalizable three-generation model with massless neutrinos; QCD theta retained
profiles.primitives: Gauge fields, chiral quark and lepton fields, and a Higgs doublet with specified representations.
profiles.machinery: SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1) gauge theory, spinors, symmetry breaking, anomaly cancellation and quantum renormalization.
profiles.choices: Conventionally 19 independent physical parameters in this specified variant: 3 gauge, 9 charged-fermion masses, 4 quark-mixing, 2 Higgs and 1 QCD theta. Neutrino masses change the count.
profiles.closure: The interaction model is specified; prediction still requires parameter calibration, state preparation and approximation control.
profiles.scope: Strong, weak and electromagnetic interactions in this model; gravity and neutrino masses are outside this row.
profiles.computation: Perturbative amplitudes and nonperturbative strong-coupling calculations pose different burdens.
profiles.comparison: A short Lagrangian hides substantial mathematical structure. EFMW has no correspondingly closed global parameter inventory in the sampled corpus.

profiles.name: Operational quantum mechanics
profiles.variant: Nonrelativistic Hilbert-space formulation with measurement postulates
profiles.primitives: States, operators, an inner product and a specified measurement procedure.
profiles.machinery: Schrodinger evolution, spectral probabilities and state-update rules.
profiles.choices: Hilbert space, Hamiltonian, preparation, observables and apparatus model.
profiles.closure: Calculationally specified for a stated system and measurement; the ontology of the measurement postulates is not fixed by this operational description.
profiles.scope: Nonrelativistic quantum predictions, not a proposed unification of gravity.
profiles.computation: The state-space size can grow rapidly with subsystem count despite a compact evolution equation.
profiles.comparison: A framework for prediction and an ontology are different comparison units; this row is included as a baseline.

profiles.name: Bohmian mechanics
profiles.variant: Nonrelativistic particle guidance with a wavefunction
profiles.primitives: Particle configuration plus wavefunction; interpretation of the wavefunction adds a further ontological choice.
profiles.machinery: Schrodinger evolution and a guidance equation; entangled states guide configurations jointly.
profiles.choices: Hamiltonian, initial wavefunction and configuration; equilibrium-distribution assumptions connect the theory to ordinary quantum statistics.
profiles.closure: The selected dynamical formulation is explicit. Relativistic or field-theoretic versions require separate specification.
profiles.scope: An alternative account of nonrelativistic quantum phenomena.
profiles.computation: Wavefunction evolution plus trajectories; adding trajectories does not remove many-body wavefunction costs.
profiles.comparison: Adds a definite state variable and law to a fixed quantum baseline; its theoretical increment is more readily isolated than the whole EFMW programme.

profiles.name: Everett relative-state quantum mechanics
profiles.variant: Unitary universal wavefunction with relative records
profiles.primitives: Universal quantum state and subsystem-relative records.
profiles.machinery: Unitary evolution and the structure of correlations; no additional physical collapse step in this formulation.
profiles.choices: Hamiltonian, initial state and the account connecting relative records and probability to experience.
profiles.closure: A compact dynamical postulate; the interpretation of probability and records must be included in an ontological comparison.
profiles.scope: Quantum foundations; the 1957 formulation does not itself supply a complete quantum-gravity model.
profiles.computation: The same large Hilbert spaces can appear as in ordinary quantum mechanics.
profiles.comparison: Many described branches do not mean many independent equations. Counting worlds is not a measure of law complexity.

profiles.name: GRW spontaneous localization
profiles.variant: Nonrelativistic discrete-collapse model; flash-ontology presentation distinguished
profiles.primitives: Wavefunction with spontaneous localization; flashes or matter density require an explicit ontology choice.
profiles.machinery: Unitary evolution between stochastic localization events; a specified localization law.
profiles.choices: Collapse rate and localization width in the usual simple model, in addition to the ordinary Hamiltonian and state choices.
profiles.closure: An explicit stochastic process after choosing the variant and its constants; field-theoretic and relativistic extensions are separate models.
profiles.scope: Quantum measurement and the microscopic-to-macroscopic transition.
profiles.computation: Stochastic wavefunction evolution and sampling; cost depends on representation and particle number.
profiles.comparison: More explicit collapse dynamics than the catalogue-level EFMW collapse functional, which still needs physical specification.

profiles.name: Perturbative superstring framework
profiles.variant: Ten-dimensional perturbative superstring formulations, as described by Schwarz (2000)
profiles.primitives: Strings, worldsheet fields and their target-space backgrounds; branes enter relevant sectors.
profiles.machinery: Worldsheet quantization, supersymmetry, anomaly constraints, mode spectra, interactions and compactification.
profiles.choices: String scale, background and compactification/vacuum data; a count of couplings alone omits major choices.
profiles.closure: Explicit perturbative calculations exist for selected backgrounds. This source does not uniquely select the observed low-energy world.
profiles.scope: A proposed framework including quantum gravity and gauge/matter sectors.
profiles.computation: Conformal/worldsheet methods, spectra and sums over worldsheet topology; background dependence matters.
profiles.comparison: Documented machinery is extensive. No shared metric establishes that EFMW is more mathematically complex than this framework.

profiles.name: Canonical loop quantum gravity
profiles.variant: Connection/holonomy and spin-network formulation in Rovelli (1998)
profiles.primitives: Gravitational connection/triad variables and quantum states represented by labeled graphs.
profiles.machinery: Holonomy-flux algebra, geometric operators and quantum constraints.
profiles.choices: Quantization and dynamical-constraint choices, states and matter coupling; the source discusses competing dynamics.
profiles.closure: Kinematics and geometric spectra are developed; the selected historical review identifies dynamics as a major open component.
profiles.scope: Nonperturbative quantization of gravitation; not a complete particle-physics fit in this selected source.
profiles.computation: Graph representation theory and constraint evaluation; finite truncations do not measure whole-theory complexity.
profiles.comparison: Discrete geometric spectra do not make the mathematical apparatus simple, and a graph count cannot be compared with EFMW equation count.

profiles.name: Causal set program
profiles.variant: Locally finite partial orders and growth models in Sorkin (2003)
profiles.primitives: Discrete events with causal ordering and local finiteness.
profiles.machinery: Order theory, stochastic growth examples and continuum-approximation questions.
profiles.choices: A dynamics or quantum measure, initial structures and a map to continuum observables; the order axioms alone do not choose these.
profiles.closure: Specified growth models are executable; the selected source distinguishes them from a completed quantum dynamics.
profiles.computation: Sampling and comparing large orders can be difficult even when the primitive definition is short.
profiles.comparison: A small ontological vocabulary can leave substantial dynamical choices. This illustrates why sparse primitives do not imply closure.

profiles.name: Causal dynamical triangulations
profiles.variant: Lorentzian triangulated gravitational path integral in the 2013 account
profiles.primitives: Causally organized triangulated geometries as a regulator of a sum over spacetimes.
profiles.machinery: Regge action, a constrained ensemble, Wick rotation in the construction, Monte Carlo and continuum limits.
profiles.choices: Bare couplings, triangulation/topology conventions, ensemble and scaling limit.
profiles.closure: Concrete finite-regulator simulations; a continuum interpretation requires scaling analysis.
profiles.scope: Nonperturbative quantum spacetime. Regulator simplices need not be interpreted as final fundamental particles.
profiles.computation: Large statistical ensembles and finite-size/continuum extrapolations.
profiles.comparison: Implementation size and a set of geometric rules measure different things; neither is comparable to the raw length of the EFMW catalogue.

profiles.name: Asymptotic safety gravity
profiles.primitives: Metric fields and a scale-dependent effective action.
profiles.machinery: Functional renormalization-group equation, gauge fixing, Ward identities and truncation of theory space.
profiles.choices: Truncation, regulator and renormalization trajectory; the complete relevant-parameter count is not supplied by one truncation.
profiles.closure: A chosen truncated flow is computable. Conclusions about the full theory require controlling truncation dependence.
profiles.scope: A possible ultraviolet completion of gravitational field theory.
profiles.computation: Coupled flows and functional/operator expansions can grow in complexity as truncations improve.
profiles.comparison: One functional equation can encode infinitely many possible operators. Printed-equation count misses this burden.

profiles.name: Noncommutative spectral-action model
profiles.variant: Chamseddine–Connes–Marcolli 2006/2007 Standard Model plus gravity construction
profiles.primitives: A spin manifold and finite noncommutative geometry represented through algebra, Hilbert space and Dirac-operator data.
profiles.machinery: Spectral action, geometric constraints and an expansion yielding gravity and particle-physics terms.
profiles.choices: Finite algebra/representation, Dirac-operator data, cutoff function/scale and associated couplings.
profiles.closure: An explicit effective action for a specified geometric construction. Its historical parameter relations are model predictions, not automatic empirical facts.
profiles.scope: An effective unification of the Standard Model with neutrino mixing and gravity.
profiles.computation: Spectral geometry, representation theory and effective-action expansion.
profiles.comparison: A compact spectral expression packages considerable structure; it supplies a concrete comparator for EFMW's proposed common action.

profiles.name: Wolfram hypergraph program
profiles.primitives: Relations or hypergraphs and rewrite rules, with causal/multiway structures built from updates.
profiles.machinery: Discrete rewriting, causal invariance and proposed links between limiting structures and physical laws.
profiles.choices: Rule, seed, updating/multiway treatment and physical-observable map.
profiles.closure: A selected rewrite system can be simulated. The framework description does not by itself choose a unique physical model.
profiles.scope: A proposed route to fundamental physics from discrete computational structures.
profiles.computation: Rule matching and growth of state histories; short rules can produce large calculations.
profiles.comparison: Like EFMW, a broad programme must be distinguished from a fully selected physical model. Shared ambition does not establish equivalence.

profiles.name: EFMW canonical corpus
profiles.variant: 102-entry catalogue plus the explicitly frozen review overlay
profiles.primitives: Proposed scalar/informational fields, metric and conventional fields, recursive state/model variables, collapse operators and additional application constructs.
profiles.machinery: Mix of tensor/PDE relations, actions, ordinary recurrences, statistical functionals and operational acceptance criteria.
profiles.choices: Functions such as F, potentials and coupling/observer maps remain task-dependent or unspecified; no single independent-parameter inventory is established.
profiles.closure: Several scoped mathematical models are encoded, but the frozen review explicitly leaves physical identification, a non-circular interpretation and key conservation/analytic obligations unresolved.
profiles.scope: Broad physics and cross-domain programme including cognition, monitoring, risk and ethics. Breadth of labels is not demonstrated unification.
profiles.computation: Some kernels are inexpensive; coupled continuum models can be expensive. A whole-theory runtime or complexity class is undefined without a fixed problem.
profiles.comparison: Best described by a heterogeneous complexity profile and open interfaces. A global complexity rank is not established.
